title: ALMA Super-resolution Imaging of T Tau: r = 12 au Gap in the Compact Dust Disk around T Tau N
question: Explore several au-scale substructures in the compact protoplanetary disks around the T Tau triple star system using sparse modeling super-resolution imaging of ALMA 1.3 mm continuum data.

data.angular_resolution: CLEAN: 0''.14 x 0''.10 (17 au); SpM effective resolution: 0''.038 x 0''.027 (5 x 4 au)
data.sensitivity: CLEAN RMS: 41 uJy beam^-1; SpM detection threshold I_DT: 272 mJy asec^-2 (152 uJy beam^-1 when convolved with CLEAN beam); SpM DIFMAP residual RMS: 31 uJy beam^-1

evidence.loc: Introduction
evidence.quote: This system consists of a star (T Tau N) in the north and a close binary (T Tau Sa and Sb) in the south (cite: Dyck1982; Koresko2000), located in the Taurus star-forming region at a distance of $143.7\pm 1.2$ pc, as measured by Gaia DR2 (cite: Gaia2016; Gaia2018).

what.value: Mass of T Tau Sa (2.1 M_sun) and Sb (0.4 M_sun)

evidence.loc: Introduction
evidence.quote: The mass of T Tau Sa and Sb are $2.1~M_{\odot}$ and $0.4~M_{\odot}$, respectively (cite: Schaefer2020).

what.value: Stellar bolometric luminosity of 6.82 L_sun and stellar mass of 2.19 M_sun for T Tau N

evidence.loc: Introduction
evidence.quote: The stellar properties of T Tau N have been calculated using optical spectral types combined with stellar evolutionary models in several studies, and we adopted a stellar bolometric luminosity of $6.82~L_{\odot}$ and a stellar mass of $2.19~M_{\odot}$ (cite: Herczeg2014).

what.value: Predicted stellar positions from the stellar orbit model of the T Tau S binary

evidence.loc: Dust Emissions from T Tau Sa and Sb
evidence.quote: To confirm whether each of the two emissions originated from T Tau Sa or Sb, Figure 2 compares the image with stellar positions predicted by the stellar orbit model of the T Tau S binary in (cite: Kohler2016), based on observational data spanning approximately 18 years.

what.value: DSHARP dust opacity model kappa_nu,I and conventional dust opacity model kappa_nu,II

evidence.loc: Physical Properties of T Tau N Disk
evidence.quote: One is DSHARP opacity model $\kappa_{\nu,\rm I}$ (cite: Birnstiel2018) assuming a maximum grain size of 0.1 mm supported by recent (sub)mm polarization measurements of other Class II PPDs in the Taurus region (cite: Bacciotti2018).

evidence.loc: Physical Properties of T Tau N Disk

what.value: Constant parameters A = 1.11, B = 0.29, C = 0.0478, D = 1.23 and gas-to-dust surface density relation for planet mass estimation

evidence.loc: Planetary Origin and Planet Mass Estimates
evidence.quote: Finally, the four parameters ($A = 1.11$, $B = 0.29$, $C = 0.0478$, and $D = 1.23$) are selected from Table 1 and 2 of (cite: zhang2018), when considering the estimated $\Sigma_{\rm g} (> 100~\rm g~cm^{-2})$ and the maximum dust particle size (cite: Bacciotti2018) in the disk.

recipe.goal: Calibrate raw ALMA data, self-calibrate, and produce CLEAN continuum image
recipe.method: Initial calibration via ALMA pipeline in CASA 5.1.1, phase center adjustment to T Tau N peak using fixvis, imaging with tclean (Briggs robust = 0.5), two rounds of phase self-calibration and one round of amplitude+phase self-calibration.
key_parameters: self-cal solution intervals: 98 s (1st phase), 49 s (2nd phase), 98 s (amp+phase)

recipe.goal: Super-resolution image reconstruction with Sparse Modeling (SpM) and evaluation of effective resolution and noise
recipe.method: Reconstruct image from self-calibrated visibilities using PRIISM ver.0.3.0 by minimizing cost function with chi-squared, l1-norm, and TSV regularizers; select optimal (Lambda_l, Lambda_tsv) via 10-fold cross-validation over 5x5 grid; evaluate effective resolution and detection threshold by injecting artificial point sources at 0''.4 north and measuring off-source noise statistics and DIFMAP residual map.

recipe.goal: Measure dust continuum positions, sizes, and fluxes of T Tau Sa and Sb
recipe.method: Apply 2D Gaussian fitting to each resolved component of T Tau S on the SpM image using CASA task imfit, and compare peak positions with stellar orbit model predictions from Kohler et al. (2016).

recipe.goal: Determine T Tau N disk geometry, radius, and radial intensity gap properties
recipe.method: Fit an ellipse to the radial peak positions of the outer ring (sampled every 1 deg, averaged in 20 deg bins, excluding PA 165-220 deg) with 5000 Monte Carlo iterations to get PA and inclination; deproject image and use curve-of-growth to find 95% flux radius r_d; azimuthally average radial intensity profile I_nu(r) and measure gap location r_gap, outer peak r_peak, gap width Delta_I, and gap depth delta_I following Zhang et al. (2018).
key_parameters: Delta_theta = 20 deg azimuthal bin; PA = 165 - 220 deg excluded; 5000 Monte Carlo iterations
assumptions: Outer ring is a perfect circle when viewed face-on

recipe.goal: Derive spectral index, brightness temperature, optical depth, dust surface density, outer ring mass, and Toomre Q of T Tau N disk
recipe.method: Calculate spectral index alpha_mm from CLEAN total fluxes at 218 and 233 GHz restored to the same beam; compute brightness temperature T_br(r) via full Planck function; fit power-law dust temperature T_d(r) = 360 (r/1 au)^-0.5 K smoothed with theta_eff to match T_br(r) at r < 5 au; calculate optical depth tau_nu(r), dust surface density Sigma_d(r) = tau_nu(r)/kappa_nu for two opacity models (kappa_nu,I and kappa_nu,II), integrate Sigma_d from r_gap to r_d for outer ring dust mass, and compute Toomre Q.
assumptions: T_d(r) = T_br(r) in optically thick inner region (r < 5 au) with power-law index -0.5
Two dust opacity models: DSHARP kappa_nu,I with s_max = 0.1 mm (Birnstiel et al. 2018) and conventional kappa_nu,II = 2.3 (nu/230 GHz)^0.4 cm^2 g^-1 (Beckwith & Sargent 1991)
Gas-to-dust ratio Sigma_gas / Sigma_dust = 100 and stellar mass M_* = 2.19 M_sun for Toomre Q

recipe.goal: Estimate mass of putative gap-opening planet in T Tau N disk
recipe.method: Fit a Gaussian to Sigma_d(r) in the gap region (r = 8-16 au) using SciPy optimize.leastsq to measure Delta_Sigma and delta_Sigma; apply two analytical planet-mass frameworks: (1) Kanagawa et al. (2015, 2016) on Sigma_d gap width and depth, and (2) Zhang et al. (2018) on intensity gap width Delta_I and depth delta_I, both combined with the Nomura et al. (2016) beam-smearing conservation relation (gap width inversely proportional to gap depth).
key_parameters: h_gap / r_gap = 0.05; alpha_vis = 10^-3 (also varied across 10^-2 to 10^-4)
Zhang et al. (2018) constants: A = 1.11, B = 0.29, C = 0.0478, D = 1.23
assumptions: Dust is well coupled to gas; planet is at r_Sigma,gap; product of gap depth and gap width is conserved against beam smearing; M_* = 2.19 M_sun; s_max = 0.1 mm

score_reason: Archival ALMA dataset is public, software versions (CASA 5.1.1, PRIISM 0.3.0) and key calibration/regularization parameters (self-cal intervals, Lambda_l = 10^5, Lambda_tsv = 10^9, 10-fold CV, N_iter = 1000) and analytical equations are explicitly stated; only minor imaging grid parameters (pixel size, image dimensions) and the exact numerical value of kappa_nu,I are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The dataset (2016.1.01164.S) and the core super-resolution imaging package (PRIISM) are both publicly available, the self-calibration and SpM regularization parameters are fully specified, and all main results (fluxes, disk geometry, gap location/width/depth, and planet mass estimates) are quantitative.
